item.title: La Société d'histoire de Toronto: HISTORITOUR - Wychwood Park et le Tollkeeper’s Cottage — Sun Oct 4, 1:30 PM — Tollkeeper’s Cottage Museum
item.description: Départ : Tollkeeper’s Cottage Museum, 750 Davenport Rd (coin nord-ouest de Bathurst et de Davenport). TTC : Métro Bathurst et autobus 7 nord jusqu’à Davenport. Stationnement sur la rue. Arrivée : Tollkeeper’s Cottage Museum Guides : Isabelle Montagnier et Johanne Roberge (en français) et Marilyn Spearin (en anglais) Wychwood Park a été fondé par Marmaduke Matthews, un peintre paysagiste qui a acheté le terrain en 1870 dans l’espoir d’y fonder une colonie d’artistes. Ce rêve ne s’est pas concrétisé, mais en 1891, avec son ami Alexander Jardine, Matthews a commencé à diviser son terrain en lotissements selon un plan bien établi. Aujourd’hui, Wychwood est une petite enclave privée sur les hauteurs de Davenport. Ses belles maisons sont un magnifique exemple du mouvement Arts and Crafts anglais. item.title: Reliable Multi-Agent Systems: Orchestration, State, and Human Approval — Thu Oct 8, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto Adding more agents does not automatically create a better system. Multi-agent solutions need clear responsibilities, controlled execution, recoverable state, and carefully designed decision boundaries.
In this session, we will extend the agent built in Episode 1 into a coordinated incident-management workflow. Specialist agents will handle triage, knowledge retrieval, impact assessment, and remediation planning. We will use Microsoft Agent Framework to demonstrate sequential, concurrent, and handoff orchestration patterns, and discuss where each pattern is appropriate.
The workflow will introduce typed state, checkpointing, failure recovery, and human-in-the-loop approval before any sensitive remediation action can continue. We will also separate deterministic application logic from agentic reasoning, showing which decisions should be handled by an AI agent and which should remain enforced by conventional code.

item.title: Vincent Lao (University of Montana) — Thu Oct 8, 12:33 PM — CITA Bridge
item.description:
Title: Nonlinear Dynamical Tides in Highly Eccentric Binaries: Application to Repeating TDEs and Hot Jupiters
Abstract: Dynamical tides exhibit chaotic growth within highly eccentric binaries (>~0.9) to reach a significant energy comparable to the binding energy. As a result, the critical separation for mass transfer, known as the Roche limit, can be significantly modified from the classical results based on equilibrium tides. Using an affine approximation, we analytically derive the nonlinear tidal coupling coefficients up to the four-mode perturbation level and apply them into the tidal evolution of a binary. This allows us to explore the onset of tidal disruption from first-principles hydrodynamical calculations. In this talk, I will discuss the implementation of this framework in two distinct systems: (1) repeating tidal disruption events (TDEs) near massive black holes, (2) high-eccentricity migration of Hot Jupiters. The Aga Khan Museum is proud to partner with Classic Legends Indian Films Festival (CLIFF) — a celebration of Indian cinema, bringing together timeless classics, acclaimed contemporary films, distinguished filmmakers, and engaging conversations. The festival honours India’s rich cinematic legacy while creating a global platform for screenings, retrospectives, cultural exchange, and dialogue between cinema, literature, and the performing arts.

item.title: Historical Society of Ottawa - Lest We Forget? An exploration of the Valour and Unequal Treatment of Algonquin who have served in Canada’s Armed Forces — Wed Oct 14, 7:00 PM — online
item.description:
Guest Speaker Lynn Gehl Ph.D, Anishinaabe Algonquin Advocate, Academic, Author & Artist Wendy Jocko Sgt. CD (Ret’d), Former Chief of the Algonquins of Pikwakanagan First Nation. Canadian Forces Veteran Details Wendy Jocko’s uncle and four great uncles served in WWI and her father and five uncles served in WWII. Wendy served for 23 years, including tours of duty in Bosnia and Croatia. Wendy’s son served in the 1st Battalion of the Royal Canadian Regiment. In Lynn Gehl’s book “Joseph Gagnon: An Algonquin World War I Veteran”, she recounts the story of her great-grandfather who, in exchange for his wartime service and sacrifices, found himself stripped of his rights as an Indigenous person, yet denied the rights accorded non-Indigenous veterans. This presentation will take place on Zoom. All are welcome. Zoom registration link below.
Source: Ontario Historical Society
